title: MiniMax API Pricing in 2026 and What Each Model Costs
summary: MiniMax API pricing shows input and output rates for each model. Compare per-token costs to determine which model suits your budget and requirements.
body_markdown:
## Routing each step to the cheapest model with Activepieces


In Activepieces, each step in a flow can call its own model, so email summaries and ticket labels can go to a cheaper model while MiniMax keeps the harder steps and you pay its rates only there.


Activepieces has an MIT-licensed core and 741 integrations in its open source monorepo, and any model API without a dedicated integration can be called through a generic HTTP step on your own provider key.


Bring-Your-Own-Key is listed by tier on the Activepieces pricing page, so the spend lands on your MiniMax account at MiniMax's rate rather than at a resale rate.


The Activepieces side of the bill is a flat plan: $0 on the free tier, which carries unlimited flows, 1,000 credits a month and up to 5 users, then Plus at $20 a month, so the platform cost stays negligible relative to model spend.


It doesn't change MiniMax's prices or plan limits. It changes how many of your steps are billed at them.


### Route by task difficulty


Put one expensive model on every step and you pay the premium on work a small model would pass, because a flow's cost is the sum of its steps.


Activepieces has a Router step that sends a run down one branch or another based on conditions you set, with an Otherwise branch for everything that matches neither, and because every plan including the free one has unlimited flows, a separate flow per route adds nothing to the platform bill.


Put a cheap classification step first, then let its output decide which branch runs.


In the canvas below, a Router has two conditional branches, each leading to its own agent step, and an Otherwise branch behind them.


*(screenshot)*


Point the simple branch at the cheapest model that passes your tests, and the branch that needs long context or heavy tool use at MiniMax.


The Otherwise branch is where you decide what unlabelled work costs, so make it the cheap default rather than the strong one.


### Cap spend and add a fallback model


Nothing about routing makes a bill bounded by itself. Set a spending limit with each model provider, and treat the flow's own failure handling as the second guard.


A step that errors or hits a rate limit can be retried, or its failure can be routed to a second model in a separate branch, so one throttled provider doesn't stall the run.


Choose the fallback for price as well as availability. A fallback that quietly costs several times the primary turns a rate-limit blip into a billing event.


Keep it on a model you have already tested on that step.
